findings.evidence: Lines 39–43 use this claim to justify the stronger hypotheses; the theorem statement at lines 131–133 indeed assumes `AnalyticAt ℂ f z`, but that assumption alone does not validate the asserted point-value sensitivity.
findings.fix: Remove this claim and describe the actual formal limitation: the available arbitrary-cycle residue theorem requires genuine differentiability/analyticity off `S`, whereas the circle theorem has a separate codiscrete-normal-form invariance lemma.
findings.issue: The claim that “a single misplaced value” on a general curve changes the integral is false: an interval integral is insensitive to changing its integrand at isolated parameter values; even when a curve revisits that value, the stated explanation does not establish a change.

summary: The module and public declarations are documented, but the module-level explanation inaccurately claims that changing a function at one point on a general curve changes its contour integral.
